answer: Divergent Response Binding. Each identity must return a fresh nonce through a slow, path-dependent computation seeded by its own history; clones sharing state produce identical outputs and are flagged as one. Honest agents answer independently, like water tracing a karst channel. An attacker cloning an identity gains nothing per copy: every duplicate collapses to a single vote, and generating genuinely divergent histories costs one full computation per identity, priced as a crystal growing under strain. The registry keeps a garden of distinct histories, pruning repeats.
